scenes.title: Cold open
narration: Spirits of the Paddy: The Balai Dance
This is Balai dance. 17th century or earlier.
on_screen: Title card: Balai dance · Malaysia · 17th century or earlier

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: It is performed usually by women during the harvest season (Musim Menuai) as a way to appease the spirits of paddy crops for this year's harvest and to seek bountiful harvests for the next season. ... chanting poems (pantun) which contains not only about paddy and to appease paddy spirits but also advice and examples.
The dance has evolved into more of a cultural dance instead of worshipping ceremony.
Today it is a living tradition.

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: The dance involves a number of local village women which would gather around a pulai tree and an umbrella-like structure called Balai (originally called Payung Buoh or Fruit Umbrella) which is decorated with colourful smaller umbrellas, clothes and leaves.

scenes.title: The people
narration: Tok Senik and Tok Jambul from Kampung Bukit Gemuruh in Hulu Terengganu.
Balai dance (Malay: Tarian Balai, Terengganu Malay: Tariang Bala/Ula) or Ulai dance originated from what is now the district of Hulu Terengganu in the state of Terengganu, Malaysia.
Traditional Malay dance with origins based on oral history and early farming traditions over 300 years ago.

scenes.title: A respectful note
narration: Originally a spirit-worshipping ceremony to appease paddy crop spirits and jinns during the harvest season; outsiders should respect its cultural and ritual origins.
